invalid.because: `primitive` is "badge", not "badges", so a consumer dispatching on the property would never match the node
`primitive` is missing altogether, leaving the class string as the only way to identify the node
the class string is missing the `qe-dv-badges` token, so `div[class~=qe-dv-badges]` would never match it
the class string carries a trailing space: the directive normalises `:class:`, so an un-normalised class is a defect rather than cosmetic
`tone` is "danger", which is outside the closed set neutral | accent | good | warn | bad
an item is missing the required `emphasis` field, so a consumer would have to invent a default
`label` is a number rather than a string
an item carries an unknown property (`colour`), which is how a typo in an item object is caught
`href` contains a space, so it is not a usable link target

a badge span repeats the item's `tone` and `emphasis` as properties, so the datum lives three times — in `items`, in the span's class tokens and again in the span. An inner node carries a class and nothing else.
a solid badge whose span content is bare text: `emphasis: "solid"` must be visible in the fallback as a single `strong` wrapper
the separator span carries " | " instead of the house middle dot, so the fallback row no longer reads as the contract says it does
`items` is empty — a row with no badges is a build error, never an empty node
the fallback children are empty, so a theme with no renderer would show nothing at all
a badge span carries `contract` and `primitive`, inventing a ninth primitive: only the root node self-describes

a badge span carries a top-level `label`: `myst-cli`'s embed transform deletes `label`, `identifier` and `html_id` from every node that is not a crossReference, cite, footnote node, captionNumber or link, so the property would vanish only once the page is embedded elsewhere

the root carries a top-level `label`; `myst-cli`'s embed transform runs `selectAll('[identifier],[label],[html_id]')` over an embedded subtree and deletes all three from every node whose type is not `crossReference`, `cite`, `footnoteDefinition`, `footnoteReference`, `captionNumber` or `link`, so the property works locally and silently disappears the first time the page is embedded elsewhere

the retired `naLabel` is carried on the root: the draft let each block spell a missing value for itself, contract 1.0 spells it one way — `null` in the properties, an em dash in the fallback — so a node still carrying the option sends a consumer looking for a string that means nothing
